questions.question: DP-SGD (Abadi et al., 2016) achieves differential privacy through which two operations on gradients?
options: Gradient scaling and momentum clipping
Per-example gradient clipping to a threshold C, followed by adding Gaussian noise with std proportional to C
Batch gradient averaging and random sign flipping
Layer-wise gradient masking and stochastic depth
questions.explanation: DP-SGD's two operations: (1) clip each per-example gradient to a maximum norm C (bounding each individual's influence), and (2) add Gaussian noise with std sigma * C to the sum of clipped gradients. The noise magnitude is calibrated so the output distribution is (epsilon, delta)-indistinguishable whether or not any single example is present.

questions.question: Why is LoRA + DP-SGD the standard 2025 configuration for private LLM fine-tuning?
options: LoRA produces lower-rank gradients that are inherently more private

Full DP-SGD of a frontier model is prohibitively expensive in per-example gradient storage; LoRA limits gradient updates to a small adapter, reducing storage requirements while DP guarantees apply to the adapter
LoRA checkpoints are smaller and easier to audit for privacy compliance
DP-SGD cannot be applied to self-attention layers; LoRA restricts updates to feed-forward layers only
questions.explanation: Full DP-SGD requires storing per-example gradients for all model parameters — impractical for frontier-scale models. LoRA (Hu et al., 2022) constrains updates to a small low-rank adapter. DP-SGD applied to the adapter is computationally feasible; the base model is held fixed and its privacy guarantees are assumed from its original training.

questions.question: The 2024-2025 tension between canary-MIA results and training-data extraction results was resolved by what insight?
options: Canary MIA was shown to be statistically invalid under the assumptions used in LLM training

The two measure different things: canary MIA asks 'is example e in D?' on inserted examples, while extraction asks what of D can be recovered — the 'most extractable' data matters for privacy and canaries under-report this
Training-data extraction only works on models without DP training; DP fully prevents extraction
Both results were found to have methodological flaws and were retracted
questions.explanation: Kowalczyk et al. (arXiv:2503.06808, March 2025) resolved the tension: canary MIA inserts synthetic examples optimized for insertion, not extraction. The 'most extractable' naturally-occurring training examples have different properties. New canary designs enable loss-based MIA without shadow models, yielding the first nontrivial DP audit of an LLM on real data.

questions.question: PMixED (arXiv:2403.15638) is an alternative to DP training. What is its key mechanism?
options: It trains multiple private models on non-overlapping data shards and averages their outputs

It provides private prediction at inference time via mixture of experts on next-token distributions — each expert sees a shard of training data and aggregation adds noise for DP, avoiding DP training entirely
It trains a separate DP-protected summarization model that compresses training data before the main model sees it
It applies DP noise to the embedding layer rather than the gradients
questions.explanation: PMixED provides inference-time DP without DP training: multiple expert models each trained on a shard of data produce next-token distributions, and the aggregation applies DP noise to the mixture. This sidesteps the utility cost of full DP-SGD training, at the cost of a different threat model and the need to deploy multiple expert models.

questions.question: What is the Differential Privacy Reversal via LLM Feedback attack?
options: An attack that reverses DP-SGD noise by using multiple queries to reconstruct training gradients
An attack that uses a DP-trained model's confidence scores as an oracle to re-identify individuals — even when outputs do not leak, confidence distributions can
An attack that breaks DP guarantees by training a shadow model on model outputs
An attack that exploits the DP accountant's rounding to recover exact training data
questions.explanation: The DP Reversal attack exploits a gap between formal DP guarantees and deployment: even a model trained with proper (epsilon, delta)-DP can leak information through its confidence scores over outputs. An adversary who queries the model with known-membership examples can use the confidence distribution as a membership signal, even when the raw outputs do not reveal training data.

questions.question: The (epsilon, delta)-DP definition states that for any two datasets differing in one example and any event S: P(M(D) in S) <= e^epsilon * P(M(D') in S) + delta. What does epsilon control in practice?
options: The maximum number of queries an adversary can make
How close the output distributions are for neighboring datasets — smaller epsilon means more noise, stronger privacy guarantee, typically at greater utility cost
The proportion of training examples that can be identified by a membership inference attacker
The probability that any single training example is included in a given batch
questions.explanation: Epsilon bounds the log-odds ratio of any output event between neighboring datasets. Smaller epsilon means the output is less distinguishable whether or not any individual example is present — stronger privacy. This typically requires more Gaussian noise in DP-SGD, which increases utility cost. The epsilon-utility trade-off is the central practical challenge.
